scope.flow: Core::swap_6269342730() no-op swap path when sqrtRatio equals sqrtRatioLimit, skipping _updatePairDebtWithNative() while msg.value ETH is sent
scope.environment: Core contract and Router swap flow with native ETH (msg.value)

statements.text: The pool is initialized at tick 0 with liquidity.
The victim submits a swap with a sqrtRatioLimit set near the current price for slippage protection, and the swap carries msg.value of 10 ether.
An attacker front-runs the victim's transaction and moves the pool price down to exactly the victim's sqrtRatioLimit.
The Router calculates value = 10 ether and calls CoreLib::swap(), sending 10 ETH to Core via call(gas(), core, value, ...).
In Core::swap_6269342730(), the condition stateAfter.sqrtRatio() != sqrtRatioLimit evaluates to FALSE.
When sqrtRatio equals sqrtRatioLimit the entire swap block is skipped, including the _updatePairDebtWithNative() call, so ETH sent via msg.value is never accounted for in the debt system.
When a swap carries msg.value ETH, the debt accounting (_updatePairDebtWithNative()) must be executed so the sent ETH is accounted for in the debt system.
A swap that would be a no-op while msg.value > 0 must not silently accept the ETH; it should revert or otherwise handle the debt accounting.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker's front-run price move is a required precondition or only one of several possible triggers (legitimate swaps can also trigger it).
The exact numeric relationship between sqrtRatioLimit and current sqrtRatio at execution time is described only via the PoC example, not as a general bound.
Whether the victim's swap is a sell/buy direction and the resulting delta values are only given for the PoC example.
